title: Enforcement Rule of the Water Leisure Safety Act
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of these Rules is to prescribe matters delegated by the Water Leisure Safety Act and its Enforcement Decree and matters necessary for their implementation.

Article 2 (Formulation of Water Leisure Safety Management Implementation Plans)
(1) A Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governor, or Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as a “Mayor/Do Governor”), or the chief of a coast guard station, shall formulate a water leisure safety management implementation plan (hereinafter referred to as an “implementation plan”) under Article 4 (4) of the Water Leisure Safety Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”) and submit it to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard by the end of February each year.
(2) An implementation plan shall include the following matters:
1. Results of implementing the preceding year's implementation plan;
2. Direction of water leisure safety management policies and detailed implementation plans for the current year;
3. Other matters necessary for water leisure safety management.
(3) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may request a Mayor/Do Governor or the chief of a coast guard station to revise, supplement, or adjust an implementation plan submitted under paragraph (1).

CHAPTER II OPERATOR'S LICENSES

Article 3 (Special Cases concerning Operator's Licenses for Foreign Nationals)
Where a foreign national operates water leisure craft at an international sporting event held in the Republic of Korea under Article 6 (1) of the Act, the following standards shall apply:
1. Types of water leisure craft: Water leisure craft under Article 2 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Water Leisure Safety Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Decree”);
2. Operating period: From 10 days before the date the international sporting event begins until 10 days after it ends;
3. Operating area: Waters of the Republic of Korea;
4. Type and scale of international sporting event: An international sporting event in which at least 2 countries participate.

Article 4 (Methods of Notifying Personal Information concerning Grounds for Disqualification from an Operator's License)
A person falling under any subparagraph of Article 6 (1) of the Decree shall, under paragraph (3) of that Article, enter personal information concerning grounds for disqualification from an operator's license in the register of notifications of operator's license disqualifications in Form 1 and notify the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard thereof. Personal information held and managed electronically may be notified by copying the file and sending it by electronic mail.

Article 5 (Public Announcement of License Examinations)
When intending to conduct a license examination under Article 8 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a “license examination”) pursuant to Article 7 (1) of the Decree, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall publish the following matters in the Official Gazette or a daily newspaper, or post them on the comprehensive water leisure information system under Article 36 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the “comprehensive water leisure information system”) and on the bulletin boards of regional coast guards and coast guard stations:
1. Date, time, and place of the license examination;
2. License examination subjects;
3. Eligibility to take the examination;
4. Documents to be submitted and submission deadline;
5. Other matters necessary for conducting the license examination.

Article 6 (Submission and Receipt of License Examination Applications)
(1) A person intending to take a license examination under Article 7 (2) of the Decree shall submit a power-driven water leisure craft operator's license examination application in Form 2 to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, attaching the following documents:
1. One photograph (3.5 centimeters wide and 4.5 centimeters high, showing the front of the upper body without a hat or similar head covering, taken within the most recent 6 months);
2. Documents classified as follows:
(a) A person under 14 years of age (under 18 for a class 1 operator's license): Documents proving that the person falls under Article 9 (1) 1 of the Act;
(b) A person eligible for exemption from a license examination: Documents proving eligibility under Article 9 (1) of the Act and Article 10 of the Decree.
(2) On receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall verify a certificate of alien registration or a certificate of reporting of domestic residence (only where the applicant is a foreign national or a foreign nationality Korean) through joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. If the applicant does not consent to verification, the Commissioner shall require submission of the relevant document.
(3) On receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall record its receipt in the register of power-driven water leisure craft operator's license examination applications in Form 3 and issue the applicant an examination admission ticket in Form 4.
(4) An examination admission ticket under paragraph (3) shall be valid for 1 year from the date of receipt of the application concerned; where the applicant passes the written part of the license examination, it shall be valid for 1 year from the date of passing that written examination.

Article 7 (Scoring Standards for Practical Examinations)
(1) The scoring standards and navigation courses for practical examinations under Article 9 (3) of the Decree shall be as specified in Annex 1.
(2) When conducting a practical examination under paragraph (1), the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall have 2 examiners board each power-driven water leisure craft used for the practical examination.
(3) A practical examination under paragraph (1) shall be scored by the examiners aboard under paragraph (2) directly entering the scores on the practical examination score sheet in Form 5.
(4) When conducting a license examination, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall prepare and manage the license examination results sheet in Form 6.

Article 8 (Application for Designation as a License Examination Exemption Education Institution)
(1) A person intending to obtain designation as a license examination exemption education institution under Article 11 (1) of the Decree (hereinafter referred to as a “license examination exemption education institution”) pursuant to paragraph (2) of that Article shall submit an application for designation as a license examination exemption education institution in Form 7 to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, attaching the following documents:
1. Documents proving that the personnel, equipment, and facility standards under Article 11 (1) 2 and Annex 5 of the Decree are met, and drawings concerning the facility standards;
2. A business plan including an education implementation plan under Article 11 (4) of the Decree;
3. A copy of the permit for occupancy, use, or other permitted activities involving public waters under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Public Waters Management and Reclamation Act or public waters falling under any subparagraph of Article 3 (1) of that Act (hereinafter referred to as “public waters and equivalent waters”);
4. Articles of association (only for a corporation; hereinafter the same shall apply).
(2) On receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall verify a certificate of corporate registered matters or a certificate of business registration through joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. If the applicant does not consent to verification of the certificate of business registration, the Commissioner shall require that document to be attached.
(3) If an institution or organization that submitted an application for designation as a license examination exemption education institution under paragraph (1) is recognized as meeting the designation standards under Article 11 (1) of the Decree, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall designate it as a license examination exemption education institution and issue a designation certificate in Form 8.
(4) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may require a license examination exemption education institution designated under paragraph (3) to display a sign identifying it as a license examination exemption education institution, made in accordance with Annex 2, at a conspicuous place within the institution.

Article 9 (Educational Operations of License Examination Exemption Education Institutions)
(1) The content, hours, and methods of education for each subject that license examination exemption education institutions must operate under Article 9 (3) of the Act and Article 11 (4) of the Decree shall be as specified in Annex 3.
(2) A license examination exemption education institution shall provide education under paragraph (1) using teaching materials reviewed by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard.

Article 10 (Requirements for Personnel of License Examination Exemption Education Institutions)
The requirements for personnel of license examination exemption education institutions and the procedure for issuing power-driven water leisure craft operator's license certificates (hereinafter referred to as “license certificates”) to persons exempted from license examinations under Article 9 (5) of the Act shall be as specified in Annex 4.

Article 11 (Notification of Administrative Dispositions against License Examination Exemption Education Institutions)
Notification of a disposition revoking designation or suspending services of a license examination exemption education institution under Article 10 (1) of the Act and Article 12 (1) of the Decree shall be made using the notice in Form 9.

Article 12 (Application for Advance Renewal or Deferral of Renewal of a License Certificate)
The application for advance renewal or deferral of renewal of a license certificate under the part of Article 13 (2) of the Decree other than its subparagraphs shall be as specified in Form 10.

Article 13 (Provision of Water Safety Education)
(1) The subjects, content, and other matters of water safety education under Article 13 (1) of the Act shall be as specified in Annex 5.
(2) An entrusted safety education institution under Article 13 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an “entrusted safety education institution”) shall provide water safety education using teaching materials reviewed by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard.
(3) An entrusted safety education institution shall issue a certificate of completion of water safety education in Form 11 to a person who completes water safety education.

Article 14 (Application for Designation as an Entrusted Safety Education Institution)
(1) A person intending to obtain designation as an entrusted safety education institution under Article 15 (2) of the Decree shall submit an application for designation as an entrusted safety education institution in Form 12 to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, attaching the following documents:
1. Documents proving that the personnel, facility, and equipment standards under Article 15 (1) 3 and Annex 7 of the Decree are met, and drawings concerning the facility standards;
2. An education implementation plan including the educational content in Annex 5;
3. Articles of association.
(2) On receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall verify a certificate of corporate registered matters or a certificate of business registration through joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. If the applicant does not consent to verification of the certificate of business registration, the Commissioner shall require that document to be attached.
(3) If an institution or organization that submitted an application for designation as an entrusted safety education institution under paragraph (1) is recognized as meeting the designation standards under Article 15 (1) of the Decree, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall designate it as an entrusted safety education institution and issue a designation certificate in Form 8.
(4) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may require an entrusted safety education institution designated under paragraph (3) to display a sign identifying it as an entrusted safety education institution, made in accordance with Annex 2, at a conspicuous place within the institution.

Article 15 (Notification of Administrative Dispositions against Entrusted Safety Education Institutions)
Notification of a disposition revoking designation or suspending services of an entrusted safety education institution under Article 14 (1) of the Act and Article 16 (1) of the Decree shall be made using the notice in Form 9.

Article 16 (Issuance of License Certificates)
(1) A person intending to renew a license certificate under Article 15 (1) 2 of the Act or obtain its reissuance under Article 15 (3) of the Act shall submit an application for renewal or reissuance of a power-driven water leisure craft operator's license certificate in Form 13 to the chief of the competent coast guard station, attaching the following documents:
1. The license certificate (except where it has been lost);
2. One photograph (3.5 centimeters wide and 4.5 centimeters high, showing the front of the upper body without a hat or similar head covering, taken within the most recent 6 months);
3. A certificate of completion of water safety education (only for renewal of a license certificate).
(2) Under Article 15 (1) and (3) of the Act, the chief of a coast guard station shall issue a power-driven water leisure craft operator's license certificate in Form 14 within 14 days from the respective dates classified as follows:
1. Cases falling under Article 15 (1) 1 of the Act: The date of passing the license examination;
2. Cases falling under Article 15 (1) 2 of the Act: The date of applying for renewal of the license certificate under paragraph (1);
3. Cases of reissuing a license certificate under Article 15 (3) of the Act: The date of applying for reissuance under paragraph (1).
(3) When issuing a license certificate under paragraph (2), the chief of a coast guard station shall record and manage the issuance in the registers classified as follows:
1. Issuance of a license certificate under paragraph (2) 1: The power-driven water leisure craft operator's license management register in Form 15;
2. Renewal or reissuance of a license certificate under paragraph (2) 2 and 3: The register of renewals and reissuances of power-driven water leisure craft operator's license certificates in Form 16.

Article 17 (Issuance of License Attestations)
(1) Where a person who has been issued a license certificate applies for a document certifying its issuance, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may issue that attestation in Korean or English.
(2) A person intending to obtain a license attestation under paragraph (1) shall submit an application for a power-driven water leisure craft operator's license attestation in Form 17 to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard.
(3) On receipt of an application under paragraph (2), the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall verify the application details and whether the license certificate was issued, and then issue the applicant a power-driven water leisure craft operator's license attestation in Form 18.

Article 18 (Standards for Revocation and Suspension of Operator's Licenses)
(1) Detailed standards for revocation and suspension of operator's licenses under Article 17 (1) of the Act shall be as specified in Annex 6.
(2) When notifying a disposition revoking or suspending an operator's license under Article 17 (1) of the Act, the chief of a coast guard station shall use the notice of revocation, suspension, or warning concerning a power-driven water leisure craft operator's license in Form 19. If the license certificate holder's address, residence, or other place for notification cannot be ascertained by ordinary means, or if the notice cannot be delivered, notification may instead be made by public announcement for 14 days on the bulletin board or website of the coast guard station having jurisdiction over the address stated in the license examination application, or on the comprehensive water leisure information system.

Article 19 (Types of Crimes Using Power-Driven Water Leisure Craft)
“Murder, robbery, or other criminal acts prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries using power-driven water leisure craft” in Article 17 (1) 3 of the Act means any of the following criminal acts:
1. Criminal acts violating Articles 4 through 9 or Article 12 (1) of the National Security Act;
2. The following criminal acts violating the Criminal Act or other relevant statutes:
(a) Murder, abandonment of a corpse, or arson;
(b) Robbery, rape, or indecent acts by compulsion;
(c) Kidnapping, abduction, or confinement;
(d) Habitual theft (limited to transporting stolen items).

Article 20 (Application for Designation as an Examination Agency)
(1) A person intending to obtain designation as an examination agency under Article 17 (1) of the Decree (hereinafter referred to as an “examination agency”) pursuant to paragraph (2) of that Article shall submit an application for designation as an examination agency in Form 20 to the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard, attaching the following documents:
1. Documents proving that the personnel, equipment, and facility standards under Article 17 (1) 2 and Annex 9 of the Decree are met, and drawings concerning the facility standards;
2. A business plan;
3. A copy of the permit for occupancy, use, or other permitted activities involving public waters and equivalent waters;
4. Articles of association.
(2) On receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall verify a certificate of corporate registered matters or a certificate of business registration through joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. If the applicant does not consent to verification of the certificate of business registration, the Commissioner shall require that document to be attached.
(3) If an institution or organization that submitted an application for designation as an examination agency under paragraph (1) is recognized as meeting the designation standards under Article 17 (1) of the Decree, the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall designate it as an examination agency and issue a designation certificate in Form 8.
(4) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may require an examination agency designated under paragraph (3) to display a sign identifying it as an examination agency, made in accordance with Annex 2, at a conspicuous place within the agency.

Article 21 (Notification of Administrative Dispositions against Examination Agencies)
Notification of a disposition revoking designation or suspending services of an examination agency under Article 18 (2) of the Act and Article 18 (1) of the Decree shall be made using the notice in Form 9.

Article 22 (Personnel Training)
(1) The following persons shall receive training provided by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard under Article 19 (1) of the Act:
1. Instructors at license examination exemption education institutions (including responsible managers performing instructors' duties);
2. Instructors at entrusted safety education institutions;
3. Examiners at examination agencies (including responsible managers performing examiners' duties).
(2) Training under paragraph (1) shall be provided for each category of trainee as follows:
1. Regular training: Training provided regularly once each year, classified as follows:
(a) Trainees falling under paragraph (1) 1 and 3: At least 21 hours;
(b) Trainees falling under paragraph (1) 2: At least 8 hours;
2. Ad hoc training: Training of not more than 8 hours, other than training under subparagraph 1, provided to trainees under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) where the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard considers it necessary.
(3) The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard shall administer a completion examination to persons who have received regular training under paragraph (2) 1 and recognize those scoring at least 60 out of 100 points as having completed regular training.
(4) Detailed matters necessary for operating regular and ad hoc training under paragraph (2) and other relevant matters shall be determined and publicly notified by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard.

CHAPTER III SAFETY OBLIGATIONS

Article 23 (Wearing Safety Equipment)
(1) A person engaging in water leisure activities shall wear a life jacket under Article 20 of the Act, and shall wear a safety helmet in addition to a life jacket when engaging in water leisure activities using a water sled under Article 2 (2) 6 of the Decree or when rafting. In either of the following cases, the safety equipment specified for that case may be worn instead of a life jacket: <Amended on June 9, 2025>
1. Engaging in water leisure activities using a surfboard under Article 2 (2) 8 of the Decree or a paddleboard under subparagraph 16 of that paragraph: A board leash (equipment connecting a surfboard or paddleboard to the ankle);
2. Traveling by water leisure craft to an underwater leisure activity area under Article 2, subparagraph 4 of the Act on Safety and Promotion of Underwater Leisure Activities in order to engage in underwater leisure activities under subparagraph 2 of that Article: A diving suit.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the chief of the competent coast guard station or the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, the Governor of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province, or the head of the competent Si, Gun, or Gu (the head of a Gu means the head of an autonomous Gu, and, for the Han River within the jurisdiction of Seoul Special Metropolitan City, means the head of the agency responsible for managing the Han River of Seoul Special Metropolitan City; hereinafter referred to as the “head of a Si, Gun, or Gu”) may, taking account of the type of water leisure activity, type of craft, weather, and other conditions, specify the type of personal lifesaving equipment, such as a life jacket, survival suit, or safety helmet, that persons engaging in water leisure activities must wear and issue instructions concerning its use. <Amended on June 9, 2025>
(3) When issuing instructions under paragraph (2), the chief of the competent coast guard station or the head of the Si, Gun, or Gu shall post their content at a conspicuous place. <Amended on June 9, 2025>

Article 24 (Exceptions to Compliance with Navigation Areas)
(1) “Engines prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries” in Article 20 (2) 1 of the Decree means the following engines, excluding engines of fishing vessels formerly used as fishing excursion boats under Article 2, subparagraph 7 of the Fishing Management and Promotion Act:
1. Engines formerly used in fishing vessels designated as management vessels under Article 27 (1) of the Fisheries Act or Article 41 (1) of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act;
2. Engines formerly used in fishing vessels approved as management vessels under Article 27 (3) of the Fisheries Act or Article 41 (3) of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act;
3. Engines formerly used in fishing vessels holding permits for demarcated fisheries under Article 40 (3) of the Fisheries Act.
(2) The navigation report under Article 20 (2) 2 of the Decree shall be as specified in Form 21.

Article 25 (Exceptions to Weather-Related Restrictions on Water Leisure Activities)
The report on activities under a special weather alert under Article 21 of the Decree shall be as specified in Form 22.

Article 26 (Reporting Long-Distance Water Leisure Activities)
(1) A person intending to engage in long-distance water leisure activities under the main clause of Article 23 (1) of the Act shall submit a report on long-distance water leisure activities in Form 23 to a coast guard agency or police agency (including submission by fax or as an electronic document through an information and communications network).
(2) “Cases prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, such as accompaniment by a safety management vessel or formation of a flotilla” in the proviso to Article 23 (2) of the Act means either of the following cases:
1. Engaging in water leisure activities while accompanying, within 500 meters, power-driven water leisure craft whose navigation area is coastal waters, offshore waters, or ocean waters under subparagraph 1 (a) of Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Registration and Inspection of Water Leisure Craft;
2. Engaging in water leisure activities by forming a flotilla of at least 2 water leisure craft equipped with communication devices capable of identifying their positions, while maintaining distances of not more than 500 meters between craft in the flotilla (200 meters between non-powered water leisure craft).

Article 27 (Reporting Accidents)
A person intending to report an accident under Article 24 (1) of the Act shall report the following matters by telephone, fax, mobile telephone text message, or similar means:
1. Date, time, and place of the accident;
2. Type of water leisure craft involved in the accident;
3. Personal details of the persons involved in the accident and the operator;
4. Damage and measures taken.

Article 28 (Cases Where Unlicensed Operation Is Permitted)
(1) “Cases prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries” in subparagraph 1 of Article 25 of the Act means cases meeting all of the following conditions:
1. A person holding a class 1 power-driven water leisure craft operator's license simultaneously supervises not more than 3 water leisure craft;
2. The water leisure craft concerned is not towing another water leisure craft;
3. The case falls under any of the following:
(a) Operating water leisure craft for a license examination;
(b) Operating water leisure craft with a passenger capacity of not more than 4 persons within the business premises of a person who has registered a water leisure business under Article 37 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a “water leisure business operator”) (excluding cases where the business operator or their personnel operate the craft with customers aboard);
(c) Operating water leisure craft for education or training provided by a school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act or a school under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
(d) Operating water leisure craft for nonprofit education or training provided by an organization related to water leisure activities that is determined and publicly notified by the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard.
(2) “Cases prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries” in subparagraph 2 of Article 25 of the Act means operating the craft with a person holding a class 1 power-driven water leisure craft operator's license or a yacht operator's license aboard together. This excludes cases where the license holder is aboard while intoxicated or under the influence of drugs in violation of Article 27 or 28 of the Act.

Article 29 (Night Navigation Equipment)
(1) A person intending to engage in water leisure activities at night under the proviso to Article 26 (1) of the Act shall have the following navigation equipment, the detailed standards for which shall be as specified in Annex 7:
1. Navigation lights;
2. An electric light;
3. Night distress signaling equipment;
4. Life jackets fitted with lights;
5. Communication devices;
6. Lifebuoys;
7. Fire extinguishers;
8. Self-igniting lights;
9. A compass;
10. A satellite navigation device.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), if the area where water leisure activities are to take place is inland waters and the head of the competent Si, Gun, or Gu recognizes that night navigation poses no danger in view of the area of the water surface, water depth, current speed, and other conditions, that authority may permit some of the navigation equipment under paragraph (1) 6 through 10 to be omitted.
(3) When permitting omission of some night navigation equipment under paragraph (2), the head of the Si, Gun, or Gu shall post the details at a conspicuous place for persons engaging in water leisure activities.

Article 30 (Adjustment of Hours for Water Leisure Activities at Night)
Under Article 26 (2) of the Act, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall adjust the hours for water leisure activities at night within the range from 30 minutes after sunset until 24:00.

CHAPTER IV SAFETY MANAGEMENT

Article 31 (Operation and Use of the Comprehensive Water Leisure Information System)
The Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard may process the following services using the comprehensive water leisure information system under Article 36 (2) of the Act:
1. Services concerning operator's licenses under Article 5 of the Act;
2. Services concerning revocation and suspension of operator's licenses under Article 17 of the Act;
3. Services concerning training of personnel of license examination exemption education institutions, entrusted safety education institutions, or examination agencies under Article 19 of the Act;
4. Services concerning reporting and management of water leisure activities under Articles 22 through 24 of the Act;
5. Services concerning management of the registration status of power-driven water leisure craft under Chapter II of the Act on Registration and Inspection of Water Leisure Craft (hereinafter referred to as the “Water Leisure Craft Registration Act”);
6. Services concerning safety inspections and issuance and reissuance of safety inspection certificates and safety inspection marks for power-driven water leisure craft under Articles 15 and 16 of the Water Leisure Craft Registration Act;
7. Services concerning training of safety inspectors under Article 20 (1) of the Water Leisure Craft Registration Act;
8. Other services the Commissioner of the Korea Coast Guard considers necessary for efficiently performing the services under subparagraphs 1 through 7.

CHAPTER V WATER LEISURE BUSINESSES

Article 32 (Applications for Registration of Water Leisure Businesses)
(1) A person intending to operate a business of renting out water leisure craft or taking persons engaging in water leisure activities aboard water leisure craft under Article 37 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a “water leisure business”) shall meet the registration standards in Annex 8.
(2) A person intending to operate a water leisure business shall submit an application for registration of a water leisure business in Form 24 to the chief of the competent coast guard station or the head of the competent Si, Gun, or Gu, attaching the following documents:
1. A drawing of the business area under subparagraph 1 (a) of Annex 8;
2. A statement of facility standards under subparagraph 1 (b) of Annex 8;
3. A list of the water leisure business operator and personnel under subparagraph 1 (c) of Annex 8 and copies of the relevant license certificates (copies of license certificates are not required where verification through the comprehensive water leisure information system is possible);
4. A statement of water leisure craft and lifesaving equipment under subparagraph 1 (d) and (e) of Annex 8;
5. A list of lifeguards or rafting guides under subparagraph 1 (g) of Annex 8 and copies of the relevant qualification certificates;
6. A copy of the permit for occupancy, use, or other permitted activities involving public waters and equivalent waters.
(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), a person intending to operate a water leisure business renting surfboards, windsurfing craft, kiteboards, or paddleboards under Article 2 (2) 8, 11, 13, or 16 of the Decree, stored on land, to persons engaging in water leisure activities (limited to cases where renters personally take away or move the rented water leisure craft) shall submit an application for registration of a water leisure business in Form 24 to the chief of the competent coast guard station or the head of the competent Si, Gun, or Gu, attaching the following documents:
1. A statement of facility standards under subparagraph 2 (a) of Annex 8;
2. A statement of water leisure craft under subparagraph 2 (b) of Annex 8.
(4) On receipt of an application under paragraph (2) or (3), the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall verify the following documents through joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. If the applicant does not consent to verification of the documents in subparagraphs 2 through 4, the authority shall require those documents to be attached:
1. A certificate of corporate registered matters;
2. A certificate of business registration;
3. An extract from the resident registration record;
4. A certificate of alien registration or a certificate of reporting of domestic residence.
(5) On receipt of an application for registration under paragraph (2) or (3), the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall grant registration unless any of the following applies:
1. Failure to meet the registration standards under paragraph (1) and Annex 8;
2. Falling under grounds for disqualification under Article 39 of the Act;
3. Violation of another restriction under the Act, the Decree, or another statute or regulation.
(6) The chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall issue a water leisure business registration certificate in Form 25 to a person whose water leisure business is registered under paragraph (5).
(7) Under the latter part of the part of Article 37 (1) of the Act other than its subparagraphs, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu may relax some of the water leisure business registration standards in Annex 8 if it is recognized that this will not impede prevention of danger, taking account of the water depth, current speed, navigation distance, type of business operation, and other conditions of the relevant premises and business area.

Article 33 (Registration of Changes to Water Leisure Businesses)
(1) A person intending to register changes to registered matters under Article 37 (2) of the Act shall submit an application for registration of changes to a water leisure business in Form 26 to the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu, attaching the following documents:
1. The water leisure business registration certificate;
2. Documents proving the changes.
(2) On receipt of an application under paragraph (2), the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall verify the following documents through joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. If the applicant does not consent to verification of the documents in subparagraphs 2 through 4, the authority shall require those documents to be attached:
1. A certificate of corporate registered matters;
2. A certificate of business registration;
3. An extract from the resident registration record;
4. A certificate of alien registration or a certificate of reporting of domestic residence.
(3) If an application for registration of changes under paragraph (1) is recognized as appropriate, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall issue a new water leisure business registration certificate reflecting the changes, or enter the changes on the registration certificate submitted under paragraph (1) and issue it.

Article 34 (Renewal of Water Leisure Business Registration)
(1) The chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall notify a person whose water leisure business is registered of the registration renewal procedure and renewal application period in advance, by 1 month before the date the validity period of the water leisure business registration under Article 38 (1) of the Act expires.
(2) A person intending to renew water leisure business registration under Article 38 (2) of the Act shall submit an application for renewal of water leisure business registration in Form 24 to the chief of the competent coast guard station or the head of the competent Si, Gun, or Gu by 5 days before the registration's validity period expires, attaching the following documents:
1. The water leisure business registration certificate;
2. Changed documents, if any changes have occurred in the documents under the subparagraphs of Article 32 (2) or (3) submitted with the application for water leisure business registration.
(3) If an application for registration renewal under paragraph (2) is recognized as appropriate, the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu shall renew the water leisure business registration and reissue the applicant's water leisure business registration certificate.

Article 35 (Reporting Temporary Closure and Other Matters)
(1) A person intending to report temporary or permanent closure of a water leisure business under Article 41 (1) of the Act shall submit a report on temporary or permanent closure of a water leisure business in Form 27 to the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu by 3 days before closure, attaching the original water leisure business registration certificate. If a disaster or another unavoidable reason prevents submission within the period under the main clause, the report may be submitted by the date of temporary or permanent closure.
(2) Where a person intending to report permanent closure under paragraph (1) also intends to report closure under Article 8 (8) of the Value-Added Tax Act, that person shall submit, together with the report under paragraph (1), a closure report in Form 9 of the Enforcement Rules of the Value-Added Tax Act, or submit an integrated closure report under Article 12 (10) of the Enforcement Decree of the Civil Petitions Treatment Act. Space of at least 5 meters in front of the air mat and at least 3 meters on each side shall be secured so that a person falling into the water does not strike an obstacle, and that space shall be marked by buoys or similar means.
(3) The air mat shall be fixed against movement by ropes or similar means, installed beneath the air mat.
(4) The jumping platform and air mat shall overlap by at least 2 meters for the safety of the person jumping from the platform.

(1) The water park shall be not more than 8 meters above the water surface.
(2) Water around the water park shall be at least 1 meter deep.
(3) Facilities for movement on foot, such as pontoons, shall be installed around the water park for prompt rescue of persons who fall into the water, and the distance between the water park and those facilities shall be at least 1 meter.

4) Emergency rescue boats shall be used to patrol the business area and save lives in accidents, and shall remain available for use at all times during business hours. This excludes cases where an operator using motorboats or sailing yachts whose navigation area is sheltered waters, coastal waters, offshore waters, or ocean waters under subparagraph 1 (a) of Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Registration and Inspection of Water Leisure Craft carries on those craft emergency rescue boats equal in number to the motorboats or sailing yachts.
5) If the chief of a coast guard station or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu recognizes under Article 32 (7) that the mooring facilities among the facility standards in paragraph 1 (b) need not be provided, emergency rescue boats shall be placed near the water for rapid use.
(g) Lifeguards or rafting guides
1) Lifeguards equal in number to emergency rescue boats shall be stationed, and, for rafting, rafting guides equal in number to rafting craft shall be stationed. For rafting craft with a passenger capacity of not more than 4 persons, the number of rafting guides determined by the head of the Si, Gun, or Gu under Article 26 (4) and (5) of the Decree shall be stationed; for water parks, one additional lifeguard shall be stationed each time the area exceeds a multiple of 660 m².
2) Where fixed inflatable tubes are provided, a separate lifeguard shall be stationed for each craft in addition to lifeguards stationed according to the number of emergency rescue boats.
3) A person holding a lifeguard or rafting guide qualification under Article 26 (1) of the Decree and working at a water leisure business shall not work at another water leisure business or similar workplace during that period.

2. Water leisure businesses under Article 32 (3)
(a) Facility standards: A place capable of storing the water leisure craft under the part of Article 32 (3) other than its subparagraphs shall be provided.
(b) Water leisure craft: The craft shall have undergone a safety check under Article 43 (1) of the Act.

■ Enforcement Rules of the Water Leisure Safety Act [Annex 9]
Requirements for Operators of Businesses Using Water Leisure Craft Not Subject to Registration and Other Relevant Persons (Related to Article 38)

1. When operating fixed inflatable tubes (blob jumps) under Article 2 (2) 14 of the Decree
(a) Air mat inflation ports, surfaces, mooring lines, and similar parts shall be inspected regularly.
(b) Only one person may jump from the platform and only one person may fall from the air mat into the water at a time.
(c) At least one attendant shall be stationed above and at least one below the jumping platform; the attendant below shall hold a lifeguard qualification.
(d) It shall be checked that users are wearing life jackets and safety helmets.
(e) Users shall be allowed to use the craft only in daytime under an attendant's supervision.

2. When operating a water leisure business under Article 32 (3)
(a) Rented water leisure craft and accessories, such as boards, board leashes, and paddles, shall be inspected regularly.
(b) Renters shall be informed of water conditions around the business premises, such as weather information, tidal currents, and dangerous terrain and objects, and safety rules (such as wearing board leashes).
(c) When informing or training renters on the water about use of the craft, precautions, and similar matters, portable lifesaving equipment, such as portable lifebuoys and rescue tubes, shall be provided for dealing with safety accidents and saving lives.

■ Enforcement Rules of the Water Leisure Safety Act [Annex 10]
Detailed Standards for Revocation of Water Leisure Business Registration and Suspension of Business (Related to Article 39)

1. General standards
(a) If there are two or more violations and their respective disposition standards differ, the heavier disposition standard shall apply. If two or more disposition standards all require suspension of business, the heavier disposition standard shall be increased by up to one-half, without exceeding the sum of the periods under the respective disposition standards.
(b) Standards for administrative dispositions based on the number of violations shall apply where an administrative disposition has been received for the same violation within the most recent 1 year. The period shall be calculated by reference to the date the administrative disposition was received for the violation and the date on which the same violation committed again after that disposition was detected.
(c) When imposing an aggravated administrative disposition under item (b), the applicable violation level shall be the level immediately following that of the disposition preceding the violation concerned (the highest level if two or more administrative dispositions were imposed within the period under item (b)).
(d) The authority imposing the disposition may reduce the business suspension period under the individual standards in paragraph 2 by up to one-half in any of the following cases:
1) Where the violation is recognized as resulting from minor negligence or error;
2) Where the violator immediately corrects or remedies the violation and thereby ends the state of noncompliance with the Act;
3) Where a reduction of the business suspension period is otherwise considered necessary in view of the nature, severity, motive, consequences, or other circumstances of the violation.
